items.question: Why not ArrayList?
items.answer: ArrayList stores object. Adding an int boxes. Reading requires a cast that can throw InvalidCastException. List<int> stores ints, the compiler rejects a string, and there is no box. Microsoft’s generics overview says always prefer System.Collections.Generic.
followUps: What is reification versus Java type erasure?
Can you add a string to List<object> that was really a List<string>?
items.sixtySeconds: ArrayList = object + boxing + casts. List<T> = compile-time T, runtime constructed type, no box for structs.

items.question: Name the important constraints.
items.answer: class, class?, struct, notnull, unmanaged, new(), a base type, an interface, Enum, Delegate, and the anti-constraint allows ref struct. new() must be last among ordinary constraints. struct and unmanaged already imply a constructor story and cannot pair with new(). notnull is a warning, not an error.
followUps: Why can’t a type with required members satisfy new()?
What does where T : U mean?
items.sixtySeconds: Constraints unlock members on T. struct/class/notnull/unmanaged are mutually exclusive as the first slot. allows ref struct is last and special.

items.question: IEnumerable<string> assigned to IEnumerable<object> — legal?
items.answer: Yes, because IEnumerable<out T> is covariant. IList<string> to IList<object> is not — you could Add a Cat to a dog list. Action<object> can be used as Action<string> (contravariance, in T). TypeScript’s default function parameter bivariance is looser; do not import that intuition.
followUps: Why arrays are covariant but generic lists are not?
Where does out T appear besides IEnumerable?
items.sixtySeconds: out = producer = covariant. in = consumer = contravariant. Mutable lists are invariant. Arrays are the historical exception.

items.question: How would you model a Redis cache miss in a generic API?
items.answer: Not T Get<T>(key) returning null — that collapses miss and stored-null. Prefer bool TryGet<T>(key, out T value) with MaybeNullWhen(false), or Result<T> with explicit Miss / Hit / Fault. That is a closed generic you control, not a BCL type.
followUps: Would you use T? on an unconstrained T?
items.sixtySeconds: Miss is not null. Use TryGet or Result<T>. Unconstrained T? is a mess across struct and class.
